LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly
2. use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives to a partner. (skill: use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly.
3. Practise this skill: use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony?
2. how much more sugar was bought?
3. Why do we ask questions?
4. How do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly.
5. Be able to: use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
